answer: One concrete defense is a bandwidth-bound rendezvous protocol. Each epoch the network pairs every agent with a random partner and a short window to exchange a signed nonce. Honest agents wander from slot to slot in real time, so their reply latency spreads irregularly, like water seeping through karst limestone. A sybil farm answering for hundreds of identities inside one window cannot avoid clustering: replies arrive at the throughput of a falcon, not a human-paced agent. Peers sample those timings and flag correlated accounts, because shared latency means shared control.
